To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aging is associated with a decrease in performance for power and endurance activities; however, the rate of decline is greater for strength than for endurance activities.

the age-related decline in power-lifing performance is greater than that in endurance rowing performance and that the rate of decline for endurance rowing performance is less than that for strength performance.
aging has traditionally been associated, with several functional declines in the musculoskeletal systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of aging on the performance of male and female master (aged) athletes in power-lifting and stationary rowing activities.
the effects of aging on performance in strength and endurance activities.
the effects of aging on male/female master athletes' performance and the effects of aging and training on the performance of male/female master rowers and power lifters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aging does not have a uniform effect on the musculoskeletal performance of master athletes, and that the effects of aging on performance are activity-specific.
the aging process has a significant impact on both strength and endurance performance in both sexes, but the rate of decline varies between the sexes and between the different activities.
the aging process does not necessarily have a negative effect on athletic performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aging is associated with declines in performance in power- and endurance activities, but that these declines are relatively slow and that the capacity for function persists throughout life in older adults who remain in good physical condition.
strength training is an important component of exercise programs for all ages and especially for older adults.

the aging process has an adverse impact on the performance of older athletes, but that this impact is not universal and that it is possible to maintain a high level of physical fitness throughout the lifespan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
strength decreases more rapidly with aging than endurance capacity.
aging is not an irreversible process.
the capacity for physical activity persists throughout life.
